question: How much will Nvidia's stock price returns exceed Apple's in these biweekly periods of Q3 2026? (Sep 21 - Oct 2)

calls.reasoning: Numeric spread of two mega-cap returns over ~10 sessions with no earnings for either name (NVDA reported Aug 26, next ~Nov; AAPL Oct 29) and no GTC (March/November). Reference class: non-earnings 10-trading-day NVDA-minus-AAPL return spreads, whose recent median is about -0.4pp per period, matching trailing-12m drift (AAPL +40% vs NVDA +26% ~ -0.5pp/biweek). Center held near zero: Apple's 12m relative momentum and its iPhone-18/foldable catalyst flow point one way, NVDA's 2.22 beta, low IV rank and recent -5.1pp 10-day lag point the other; at a two-week horizon neither is worth more than a fraction of a point. Dispersion dominates - clean non-earnings windows in this very sample ran -15.0pp and +13.1pp - so I spread the percentiles to ~17pp 10-90. Open bounds priced at 4% each side: a DeepSeek/tariff-style AI-capex or AI-safety shock (NVDA fell 3.4% in a day on Sep 14 on Amodei frontier-model comments) takes the spread below -15; a mega AI deal or supply headline plus an Apple sell-the-news reversal takes it above +15. No matching market exists; Polymarket's Dec-31 largest-company contract (NVDA 61%/AAPL 23.5%, ~$4.5M vol) differs on quantity, horizon and resolution source, so I used it only as context, not as an anchor.

calls.reconciliation: Five disputes. (1) Non-earnings dispersion, part factual: Run 1 counts Jul 14-Jul 28 = -15.0pp as a clean window while Run 3 attributes that same extreme to earnings and Run 2's sample starts Aug 7 so never sees July. On the earnings dates the dossiers themselves give (AAPL ~Jul 30, NVDA Aug 26), a window ending Jul 28 contains neither report, so Run 1's classification is the consistent one; I could not re-pull the series to verify the -15.0 value itself, so it carries residual uncertainty, but it tips the reconciled dispersion wide. (2) Pairwise correlation, factual but UNSETTLED: Run 2 computed -0.21 ex-earnings, Run 1 read +0.2 to +0.4, Run 3 found no published figure and assumed 0.35-0.55; no vendor number exists in any dossier and I had no web access. All three do agree on the mechanism (AI-vs-consumer rotation days: Sep 9 NVDA -2.4%/AAPL +3.6%, Sep 14 NVDA -3.4%/AAPL +0.2%), which is what produces low-to-negative readings, so I used 0.1-0.3 rather than picking a side by fiat. (3) iid-scaled 8.0pp vs realized-overlapping 4.6pp vs IV-implied 6.0-7.0pp, judgment: the overlapping statistic has roughly four independent observations and is autocorrelated, so it is the weakest of the three; I took 6.1pp, near IV-implied at low correlation. (4) Escape mass, judgment: Run 1's 4% per side is hard to square with NVDA's IV rank of 8, and Runs 2/3's 2% is hard to square with a Gaussian-plus-fat-tail read of a 2.5 SD move in a regime that just produced a 6% one-day semis drawdown; I set 3% down / 2.5% up, asymmetric because the identified mechanism is directional. (5) Center: all three runs land -0.2 to -0.5 and I carried that forward at -0.3, treating the six-week -3.5pp mean as momentum rather than forecastable drift. Undisputed and adopted without change: 10 sessions, no in-window earnings or GTC, Duo catalyst after the window, quarter-end Sep 30, and no matching prediction market in any venue. My width lands outside all three runs rather than between them because the dispersion evidence resolves in Run 1's direction while its tail pricing does not.

disagreements.claim: 10-day spread SD is ~4.6pp (realized overlapping) vs ~6-7pp (options-implied) vs 8.0pp (iid-scaled daily)
disagreements.verdict: Took 6.1pp. The 4.6pp overlapping figure rests on about four independent windows and is downward-biased by autocorrelation; the 8.0pp iid scaling ignores observed mean reversion; IV-implied at low correlation sits between and is the least sample-dependent.

disagreements.claim: Probability of the spread escaping the +/-15 band is ~4% per side vs ~2% per side
disagreements.verdict: Settled at 3% below / 2.5% above. NVDA's IV rank of 8 is genuine evidence against Run 1's 4%; the live AI-safety shock channel and the observed 6% one-day semis drawdown argue against Runs 2/3's 2%, and make the low side the fatter one.

disagreements.claim: Center of the distribution: -0.2 vs -0.2 vs -0.5
disagreements.verdict: No material disagreement; all three cluster near zero-minus-a-fraction. Adopted -0.3, with the negative 12-month relative drift roughly offset by NVDA's beta advantage against positive equity drift.

disagreements.claim: Whether any prediction market anchors this question
disagreements.verdict: Unanimous across runs and confirmed against the harness candidate list: none matches. Polymarket's largest-company-end-2026 prices a market-cap ranking at a Dec 31 deadline and the Manifold candidate is big-tech-vs-Bitcoin closing 2030. Neither used as an anchor.
